docs.title: auditor
docs.text:
auditme, a static checker that projects pin as pre-commit hooks so the rules a script can check are enforced on every commit, push and CI run, together with the Claude Code Stop hook that runs it before a turn ends, the /auditme-project-setup skill that adopts the hooks in a project, and the Python rules the checker enforces. The other shared rules and skills live in the agents repository (bnomis/agents).

git clone https://github.com/bnomis/auditor.git $AUDITOR_PATH
$AUDITOR_PATH/bin/install-claude.sh

The installer links the /auditme and /auditme-project-setup skills and the Stop hook into ~/.claude/, and registers the Stop hook. A project then opts in to the checker with /auditme-project-setup new or /auditme-project-setup adopt, which pins the hooks in its .pre-commit-config.yaml:

- repo: https://github.com/bnomis/auditor
  rev: <commit>
  hooks:
    - id: auditme-changed
    - id: auditme-all
      stages: [manual, pre-push]

docs.title: What is in the repository
docs.text: Path What it is src/auditor/ The checker, run as auditor: a standard-library-only sweep over src/ and bin/. See The audit checker. claude/skills/auditme/ The /auditme skill: the sweep, then the interpretive review. See Skills. claude/skills/auditme-project-setup/ The /auditme-project-setup skill and its templates. See Skills. src/auditor/catalogue/rules/std-*/ The Python standards the checker enforces: coding standards, imports, dependencies. See Rules. claude/hooks/ The Claude Code Stop hook that runs the checker before a turn ends. bin/install-claude.sh The installer: runs the shared install-in-claude at a pinned commit. See Command line and hooks. bin/install-hooks.sh Adds the audit hooks to a project's .pre-commit-config.yaml, or moves them to the latest commit, and installs the git hooks. See Command line and hooks. bin/check-foreign-names.sh The no-project-names check, which keeps project names out of repositories used across projects. See Command line and hooks. .pre-commit-hooks.yaml The hooks other projects pin.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read How it works for the moving parts and why each is where it is.
  2. Follow Setting up for a new machine, a new project or an existing one, or to move a project that still pins bnomis/agents.
  3. Read The audit checker before the first hit appears: what it sweeps, how to read a hit and how to accept one.
  4. Look things up in the reference: Skills and Command line and hooks.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• A rule a script can check is a hook. A rule that lives only in prose drifts; the checker turns each mechanical rule into a failing commit, so the drift never reaches an audit.
  • The commit sees your changes; the push sees everything. The commit hook reports hits only in the files a commit changes, so nobody is blocked by someone else's old hit; the push gate and CI sweep the whole tree.
  • Projects choose when to upgrade. Each project pins the checker to a commit of this repository, so a new rule fails a build only after pre-commit autoupdate.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The repository has two consumers: each project's pre-commit and CI, which run the checker pinned to a commit of this repository, and Claude Code on your machine, which runs the Stop hook from ~/.claude/.

flowchart LR
    repo["auditor repository"]
    home["~/.claude/<br>auditme, auditme-project-setup, Stop hook"]
    proj["project<br>.pre-commit-config.yaml"]
    ci["project CI"]
    repo -- "bin/install-claude.sh<br>(symlinks)" --> home
    repo -- "rev: <commit>" --> proj
    proj -- "pre-commit run" --> ci

docs.title: The checker in a project
docs.text:
The checker is the auditor package (src/auditor/), installed as the auditor command: Python with no dependencies outside the standard library, plus ruff and uv for the hygiene checks and git for the commit hook's diff. A project pins it through .pre-commit-hooks.yaml:

Where Hook Scope Fails on git commit auditme-changed the whole tree is swept, hits are reported for files changed on the branch (<base>...HEAD) or in the index or working tree; the sweep is skipped when no diff base resolves or no reportable file changed an unaccepted hit in a changed file, or in a file a cross-file hit links to one; or a failure: git cannot run, a git diff or rev-parse fails, the repository root cannot be resolved, or the sweep cannot start, times out, exits non-zero, prints a line that is not a hit or reports a crashed check git push auditme-all (a manual-stage hook: the project's config adds pre-push to run it at push) the whole tree any unaccepted hit CI auditme-all the whole tree any unaccepted hit

The commit hook ignores hits in files you did not touch, so an old hit never blocks an unrelated commit. The push gate and CI catch what the commit hook cannot see: a hit that appears without its file changing, such as a duplicate of code added elsewhere.

A hit you have judged correct to keep is accepted in the code, beside the hit, with the reason:

# auditme: accept[<rule>] <reason>

The reason stays in the source, where the next reader of that line sees it. See The audit checker for the rules and the marker's exact placement.

docs.title: Pinning and upgrades
docs.text:
Projects pin the hooks with rev: to a commit of this repository. A new rule therefore fails no build until a project upgrades with pre-commit autoupdate, and the upgrade commit fixes or accepts the new hits in the same change. This repository runs its own hooks from its working tree (repo: local), so a checker change applies in the commit that makes it.

A project that adopted the hooks before the checker moved here still pins bnomis/agents. That pin keeps working, because the agents commits it names still hold the checker; see Moving a project from agents.

docs.title: Rules repositories and trust
docs.text:
The checks and the Phase B questions can live in a separate rules repository that AUDITOR_RULES_PATH names. The runner (auditor check, auditor phaseb) loads it and runs what it holds: each rule is a directory with a rule.md and a rule.toml, and auditor-rules.toml at the root names the helper API version the repository was written for. auditor rules reports on it (commands).

A rules repository is trusted code. auditor check imports and runs Python from it, in the same way a project's own conftest.py runs under pytest. The runner loads a rules repository only from AUDITOR_RULES_PATH, never from a path the audited project names, so auditing a project cannot make the runner run that project's code as rules. Point the variable only at a repository you trust. See setup.

docs.title: The Stop hook
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh also registers claude/hooks/auditme-stop.sh as a Claude Code Stop hook in ~/.claude/settings.json. In a project whose .pre-commit-config.yaml contains id: auditme-changed, it runs the checker over the changed files when Claude ends a turn, and sends the hits back once, so Claude fixes them before handing over. Elsewhere it does nothing.

The Stop hook runs the checker from your clone, not the project's pinned revision, so it is an early warning; the pinned hooks remain the authority.

docs.title: Setting up the shared guards
docs.text: This guide takes you from nothing to a project whose commits and CI run the shared audit checks. It covers a new machine, a new user, a new project and an existing one.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• auditme-changed - a pre-commit hook. It sweeps the whole tree with the auditme checker, then fails the commit on any unaccepted hit in a file the commit changes, or in a file a cross-file hit names as related to one.
  • auditme-all - the same sweep reported over every file. It is published at the manual stage, and a project with no unaccepted hits also runs it on every push and in CI, so a hit in a file nobody touched still fails the push.
  • A Stop hook - a Claude Code hook that blocks the end of a turn once while an opted-in project's changed files carry unaccepted hits.
  • /auditme-project-setup - a skill that writes the config, CI workflow and project files for a new project, or adopts the hooks into an existing one.

The checker audits the packages under src/<package>/ and the scripts in bin/. src/ is optional: a project with only bin/ is audited over bin/, and a project with no Python at all gets only the project-level checks: its uv.lock against pyproject.toml, its ruff-pre-commit pin against the ruff the audit runs, and its Markdown (spec-api-signature-drift). A .py file directly in src/ belongs to no package, so it is reported as a src-loose-module hit; move it into a package, or accept it with a line-1 marker. No other directory's Python is swept.

A project whose Python lives elsewhere declares its roots in pyproject.toml instead, and the declared list replaces src/ and bin/:

[tool.auditme]
roots = [
    { path = "tools/mypkg" },
    { path = "tools", modules = "top-level" },
    { path = "tests" },
]

A directory that is not declared is not swept. See auditor check for the modules values and the errors.

The checker also reads files outside those passes:

  • every .md file under the project, outside hidden directories and .git, .venv, node_modules, __pycache__, audit-reviews and tasks, for function signatures in a spec that no longer match the code (spec-api-signature-drift);
  • pyproject.toml and uv.lock (lockfile-drift), .pre-commit-config.yaml (ruff-version-drift) and AGENTS.md, which declares project standards some rules enforce.

The checker's rules are described in The audit checker and in claude/skills/auditme/SKILL.md.

docs.title: Why the scopes differ
docs.text: The commit hook looks at changed files only, so a commit is never blocked by someone else's old hit. CI looks at the whole tree, so a hit that appears without touching its file (a cross-file duplicate, say) is still caught. A cross-file hit counts as changed when either of its files changed.

docs.title: Why the checker is pinned
docs.text: Projects pin the hooks to a revision of this repository (rev: in .pre-commit-config.yaml). A new rule therefore never fails a build until you choose to upgrade (see Upgrading the checker).

docs.title: Why the Stop hook is global
docs.text: The Stop hook is registered once, in ~/.claude/settings.json, and does nothing in a project whose .pre-commit-config.yaml lacks id: auditme-changed. It runs the installed auditor command, not the project's pinned one, so it is an early warning and the pinned hook stays the authority. In a worktree of the auditor checkout recorded in ~/.claude/auditor-source, it runs that worktree's own checker instead, so a branch that changes the checker is judged by its own version. No other repository's copy of the checker is ever run.

docs.title: A new machine
docs.text:
Prerequisites:

  • git
  • gh, authenticated: gh auth login
  • uv, from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/
  • pre-commit: uv tool install pre-commit
  • Python meeting requires-python in pyproject.toml; the hooks run with the python3 their shebang finds on PATH
  • jq, used by the Stop hook
  • ruff, which the checker runs: the executable AUDITME_RUFF names when that variable is set (for a ruff outside the project's .venv); otherwise the project's own .venv/bin/ruff when it exists (after uv sync), whatever else is on PATH; otherwise ruff from PATH, such as uv tool install ruff. Without either, a sweep that audits a package or extra root reports ruff not installed; a project with no audit root runs only the project-level checks and does not. It must be the version the ruff hook's rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml pins; otherwise the sweep reports ruff-version-drift. Make them equal with uv add --dev ruff==<version>, or change the hook's rev

Install:

git clone https://github.com/bnomis/auditor.git <directory>
cd <directory>
bin/install-claude.sh

<directory> is wherever you keep your source. The script first installs the checker as the auditor command (uv tool install --editable <directory>) and records this repository's git directory in ~/.claude/auditor-source, which the Stop hook reads. It then runs the shared installer, install-in-claude, with uvx at a pinned commit, so it needs uv and SSH access to bnomis/install-in-claude; add --dry-run to see what it would change first. It links claude/ into ~/.claude/ one level down: each directory (hooks/, rules/, skills/) becomes a real directory of symlinks to its entries. It renames any existing file in a link's place to .orig. In ~/.claude/settings.json it adds the Stop hook once. It keeps every other setting, and saves the original as settings.json.orig. It refuses to touch a settings file that is not a valid JSON object.

The other shared rules and skills, and the status line, come from the agents repository (bnomis/agents), installed the same way with its own installer; see its docs at https://bnomis.github.io/agents/.

Check it:

auditor --version
ls ~/.claude/skills
grep -n 'auditme-stop.sh' ~/.claude/settings.json

Without Claude Code, install only the checker, from a release tag:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/bnomis/auditor@<tag>

<tag> is a release tag of this repository. The checker runs as auditor check, auditor changed and auditor phaseb.

docs.title: A new user
docs.text:
This repository, bnomis/auditor, is public: cloning it and running its hooks needs no access grant and no SSH key.

The shared rules and skills in the agents repository hold nothing specific to one project. A project's own rules and skills go in its claude/ directory (claude/rules/, claude/skills/); see the agents repository's claude/rules/rule-scope.md.

docs.title: A new project
docs.text:
In an empty repository, in Claude Code:

/auditme-project-setup new

It asks for the project's test command, then writes:

  • .pre-commit-config.yaml - ruff, shellcheck and both audit hooks, pinned to the current main of this repository, with auditme-all also run on push
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml - tests, the commit-time checks over the whole tree, and auditme-all
  • AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, TODO.md, DONE.md and claude/rules/README.md

It installs the git hooks with pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push.

docs.title: No key in CI
docs.text: The hooks are pinned by their HTTPS URL, https://github.com/bnomis/auditor, and this repository is public, so pre-commit clones it in CI without a deploy key or secret. The workflow needs no step for it.

docs.title: An existing project
docs.text:
/auditme-project-setup adopt

It adds the two hooks to .pre-commit-config.yaml, and shows you any project-local runner or Stop hook doing the same job before asking to remove it.

Then it counts unaccepted hits by rule over the whole tree:

pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files
  • No hits: it runs auditme-all on push as well, adds the CI step.
  • Hits: it files one TODO.md item with the dated count by rule, and leaves the push stage and CI alone. Fix or accept every hit, then enable both.

A hit is accepted with a comment on its line or the line above:

# auditme: accept[<rule>] <reason>

Why no gate over a backlog: a gate that fails every push gets switched off.

docs.title: Without Claude Code
docs.text:
bin/install-hooks.sh in this repository does the hook part of adopt from a shell: it adds the auditor entry to the project's .pre-commit-config.yaml (or creates the file), pinned to the current main of bnomis/auditor, and installs the git hooks:

$AUDITOR_PATH/bin/install-hooks.sh --dry-run <project>
$AUDITOR_PATH/bin/install-hooks.sh <project>

<project> is a path inside the project's repository; leave it out to use the current directory. The first command prints the change; the second makes it. Add --push once the project has no unaccepted hits, so auditme-all runs on every push too. The script does not count the backlog, add the CI step. See bin/install-hooks.sh for every option.

To enable the gates later, add stages: [manual, pre-push] under - id: auditme-all in .pre-commit-config.yaml, paste claude/skills/auditme-project-setup/templates/ci-audit-step.yml into the workflow after the project's own setup.

docs.title: Moving a project from agents
docs.text:
A project that adopted the hooks while the checker lived in the agents repository pins git@github.com:bnomis/agents.git. That pin keeps working until the project is moved: the agents commits it names still hold the checker, so its hooks and CI run as before. They get no new rules or fixes, which land only here.

To move it:

  1. In .pre-commit-config.yaml, change the audit hooks' repo: from git@github.com:bnomis/agents.git to https://github.com/bnomis/auditor, and their rev: to a commit of this repository: git ls-remote https://github.com/bnomis/auditor refs/heads/main, first field. The hook ids are unchanged.
  2. In the CI workflow, replace the agents deploy-key steps with the single step in claude/skills/auditme-project-setup/templates/ci-audit-step.yml, and delete the project's AGENTS_DEPLOY_KEY secret once CI passes (see Dropping the deploy key).
  3. Run pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files, and fix or accept any new hits in the same commit, as for an upgrade.
  4. If the project also pins the no-project-names hook from bnomis/agents, move it into the auditor block beside the audit hooks, keeping its args:. It moved here too, and the agents repository no longer publishes it.

The old deploy key on bnomis/agents can then be removed.

docs.title: Dropping the deploy key
docs.text:
A project set up before this repository was public pins the hooks by SSH (git@github.com:bnomis/auditor.git), and its workflow installs an AUDITOR_DEPLOY_KEY secret so the runner can clone over SSH. An SSH clone needs a key even from a public repository, so the URL changes first:

  1. Run $AUDITOR_PATH/bin/install-hooks.sh <project>, or change the auditor entry's repo: to https://github.com/bnomis/auditor by hand. The script moves an SSH entry to the HTTPS URL and reports cloned from https://github.com/bnomis/auditor.
  2. In the CI workflow, delete the Install the audit deploy key and Remove the audit deploy key steps, leaving the Audit the whole tree step as in claude/skills/auditme-project-setup/templates/ci-audit-step.yml.
  3. Commit, push, and check that CI passes.
  4. Delete the project's secret: gh secret delete AUDITOR_DEPLOY_KEY --repo <owner>/<project>.
  5. Remove the project's deploy key from this repository: list them with gh repo deploy-key list --repo bnomis/auditor, then gh repo deploy-key delete <id> --repo bnomis/auditor.

docs.title: Upgrading the checker
docs.text:
pre-commit autoupdate --repo https://github.com/bnomis/auditor
pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files

Or, from this repository, bin/install-hooks.sh <project>: it moves the auditor entry's rev: to the current main and changes nothing else in the file.

A new rule can report hits in code that passed before. Fix or accept them in the same commit as the upgrade, so main never carries a failing gate.

docs.title: Pointing the runner at a rules repository
docs.text:
The runner loads its checks from the rules repository that AUDITOR_RULES_PATH names. Set it per project with direnv, in the project's .envrc:

export AUDITOR_RULES_PATH=/absolute/path/to/your/rules-repository

Then run direnv allow and check it with auditor rules list. The repository is trusted code: the runner imports and runs it (see How it works). The runner holds no rules of its own: while the variable is unset, every command exits 2 with ERROR: AUDITOR_RULES_PATH is not set.

docs.title: Create a rules repository
docs.text:
The runner ships a catalogue of default rules, grouped into packs. To start a rules repository from it:

auditor rules packs
auditor rules init ~/src/my-rules --pack imports --pack security

init writes ~/src/my-rules/selection.txt, a list of rule names. The rules of the packs you named are uncommented and the rest are commented out; with no --pack, every pack is selected. Edit the file to comment out the rules you do not want, then:

auditor rules apply ~/src/my-rules

apply copies the uncommented rules and their tests into ~/src/my-rules/rules, writes auditor-rules.toml, README.md, TODO.md, DONE.md and .gitignore, starts a git repository there (unless the directory is already inside a work tree) and runs auditor rules check on the result. The copy is plain: the new repository keeps no link to the catalogue, so later catalogue fixes reach it only when you copy them by hand. Then add the AUDITOR_RULES_PATH line above to the project's .envrc.

docs.title: Upgrading a project that pins the hooks
docs.text:
Releases before 0.3.0 ran built-in rules when the variable was unset. From 0.3.0 the same rules ship as the default catalogue, src/auditor/catalogue, and a project must name a rules repository. To keep the previous behaviour:

  1. Create a rules repository: auditor rules init <dir> (see the CLI reference). To start from the default rules, copy src/auditor/catalogue from this repository into it.
  2. Add the variable to the project's .envrc, then run direnv allow:
export AUDITOR_RULES_PATH=/absolute/path/to/your/rules-repository
  1. Set it in CI, in the job that runs the audit hooks:
env:
  AUDITOR_RULES_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/rules-repository

The CI job must have the rules repository checked out at that path. 4. Check it: auditor rules list exits 0 and lists the rules.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The hook cannot clone this repository. Run git ls-remote https://github.com/bnomis/auditor refs/heads/main. If it fails, GitHub is unreachable from that machine. If CI fails with Permission denied (publickey), the project still pins the SSH URL: see Dropping the deploy key.

The Stop hook does not fire.

  • The project is not opted in: its .pre-commit-config.yaml must contain id: auditme-changed.
  • jq is missing: command -v jq.
  • The installer has not run: grep -n 'auditme-stop.sh' ~/.claude/settings.json.
  • No diff base resolves (no upstream, origin/main or main): changed.py prints that and passes without sweeping. Check git rev-parse --verify origin/main.
  • No reportable file changed, so changed.py skipped the sweep.
  • The directory is not a git repository: the Stop hook finds no repository root and exits 0 itself, without running changed.py.

Hits appear only after an upgrade. Expected: the new checker has new rules. See Upgrading the checker.

One commit must go through.

SKIP=auditme-changed git commit

The push and CI still sweep the whole tree, so the hit must be fixed or accepted before they pass. For one push, SKIP=auditme-all git push.

docs.title: The audit checker
docs.text:
auditor check .

The checker is the mechanical half of the auditme skill: a static sweep, written against the standard library only, that parses each file and prints one JSON object per hit. It reports; it never decides. Triage is the reviewer's job, and acceptance is the accept marker's.

It needs Python 3.14 or later. The ruff and ruff-version-drift rules run the ruff named by the AUDITME_RUFF environment variable when it is set, else the project's .venv/bin/ruff when that is executable, else ruff from PATH, and lockfile-drift runs uv lock --check. Set AUDITME_RUFF to the path of a ruff outside the project's .venv, for example one a CI job installs elsewhere:

AUDITME_RUFF=/opt/tools/ruff-0.17.4/bin/ruff auditor check .

A value that is not an executable file stops the sweep with exit 2.

docs.title: What it audits
docs.text:
Every path is relative to the project root passed as the first argument.

  • Packages under src/<package>/: each package is audited in its own pass, so module names are built without a src. prefix. src/ is optional.
  • Declared roots: when [tool.auditme] in pyproject.toml declares roots, those are the swept roots, in place of the packages and extra roots below.
  • Scripts in bin/: the default extra root, used when it exists and holds .py files. --extra-root replaces the default set.
  • A .py file directly in src/: it belongs to no pass, so it is reported as a src-loose-module hit.
  • Markdown: every .md file under the root is read for spec-api-signature-drift, except those in a hidden directory or in a .git, .venv, node_modules, __pycache__, audit-reviews or tasks directory.
  • Project files: pyproject.toml with uv.lock and .pre-commit-config.yaml are read by the project-level checks (see Project-level checks); AGENTS.md is read only by per-root checks (the gated rules and the import rules).

No other directory is swept.

docs.title: auditor check: the full report
docs.text:
auditor check <project-root> [--package <pkg>] [--extra-root <dir> ...]
Flag Effect --package <pkg> Audit only src/<pkg>/. Drops the extra roots and the src-loose-module report too. For re-checking one package while verifying a fix; a normal audit passes neither flag. --extra-root <dir> Audit <dir> (relative to the root) as its own pass. Repeatable. Replaces the default set (bin/). A named root that does not exist is an error, not an empty pass.

auditor check prints every hit, accepted or not, and exits 0 whatever it finds. It exits 2 on a usage error from argparse (an unknown option or a missing value); when the root is not a directory; when --package is not a plain directory name; when a named extra root is outside the root or is not a directory; when the --package directory is missing or is a file; or when [tool.auditme] in pyproject.toml is invalid. A project with no package and no extra root prints a note on stderr and exits 0.

docs.title: auditor changed: the gate
docs.text:
auditor changed           # changed files only
auditor changed --all     # every file

auditor changed [--all] [--base <ref>] [<repo-root>] runs auditor check over the whole tree, so cross-file rules see every file, then keeps the unaccepted hits in scope. It exits 1 when any remain, or on any failure: an argument error, a --base that is a flag, git that cannot run, a diff or rev-parse that fails, a repository root that cannot be resolved, or a sweep that cannot start, times out, exits non-zero, prints a line that is not a JSON object, or reports a crashed check. It exits 0 otherwise. A sweep that cannot run is never skipped.

Mode Scope Runs as default Files changed in <base>...HEAD, plus tracked files changed in the index or working tree against HEAD (an untracked file is in scope once staged). A hit is in scope when its path, or any of its related paths, is. The auditme-changed pre-commit hook --all Every file The auditme-all hook: the push gate and CI

--base defaults to the first of @{upstream}, origin/main and main that resolves. A value starting with - is refused, whichever spelling of the option gave it, so it is never read by git as an option. With none, or with no reportable file changed (a .py file, a uv.lock, or a .md file outside hidden directories and outside audit-reviews and tasks, among others), it prints why and exits 0 without sweeping. <repo-root> defaults to the working directory's git top level.

To see which lines changed rather than which hits remain, --scope runs no sweep and prints one JSON line per changed .py or .sh file:

auditor changed --scope --base <commit>

Each line is {"path": ..., "ranges": [[start, end], ...]}. A Python range is a diff hunk widened to its enclosing function, else its enclosing class; a shell range is the hunk. The audit skill gives these ranges to its sampled reviewers between whole-tree audits, so a small edit does not reopen a whole file.

The same runs through pre-commit:

pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files

To let one commit or push through, SKIP=auditme-changed git commit or SKIP=auditme-all git push.

docs.title: Reading the output
docs.text:
auditor check prints one JSON object per line, keys sorted:

{"accepted": false, "accepted_reason": null, "evidence": "except Exception:", "line": 9, "path": "src/pkg/core.py", "rule": "silent-broad-except", "variant": "no logger and no raise in body"}
{"accepted": true, "accepted_reason": "best-effort read of an optional cache", "evidence": "except Exception:", "line": 17, "path": "src/pkg/core.py", "rule": "silent-broad-except", "variant": "no logger and no raise in body"}
{"accepted": false, "accepted_reason": null, "evidence": "def load(path, strict): | src/pkg/core.py:6", "line": 6, "path": "docs/spec.md", "related": ["src/pkg/core.py"], "rule": "spec-api-signature-drift", "variant": "load: spec says (path, strict), source says (path)"}
Key Meaning rule The rule id (see The rules) variant Which form of the rule fired, or a summary of this hit path Repository-relative path, or null for a hit with no file line 1-based line, or null evidence The source snippet or identifier that matched accepted true when an accept marker or, for in-function-import only, an AGENTS.md row covers the hit; an AGENTS.md row for layering-violation makes the check print no hit at all accepted_reason null for a hit that is not accepted; otherwise the marker's reason, no reason given for a marker with none, or AGENTS.md accepted (<importer> -> <imported>) for an in-function-import hit an AGENTS.md row covers related Only on a hit that compares files: the other files' paths, sorted, never the hit's own

Identical hits are printed once, so a hit that several passes would each report appears once.

auditor changed prints only unaccepted hits in scope, sorted by path and line, as <path>:<line> <rule> with the variant indented beneath, then how to fix or skip:

src/pkg/core.py:9  silent-broad-except
    no logger and no raise in body

Fix each hit, or accept one with a comment on its line or the line above:
    # auditme: accept[<rule>] <reason>
To skip this check for one commit: SKIP=auditme-changed git commit

docs.title: Accepting a hit
docs.text:
Fix the hit, or accept it with a comment on the hit's line or the line above:

def other(path):
    try:
        return open(path).read()
    # auditme: accept[silent-broad-except] best-effort read of an optional cache
    except Exception:
        return None

The marker matches # auditme: accept[<rule>] <reason> anywhere on the line, so it can follow code or a # noqa. A few rules (from-import, except-interpolation, spec-api-signature-drift) also take a marker on any line of a statement that spans several lines.

  • Scope it to a rule. accept[<rule>] answers only for that rule; a hit from another rule on the same line stays unaccepted. The unscoped form, # auditme: accept <reason>, answers for every rule on the line, including rules added after it was written, so write new markers scoped.
  • One marker per rule. A line that two rules hit can carry two scoped markers, # auditme: accept[rule-a] <reason> # auditme: accept[rule-b] <reason>; each reason ends where the next marker begins.
  • Give a reason. It is copied into accepted_reason and is what a reviewer reads instead of re-arguing the hit.
  • Line-1 markers. src-loose-module is reported at line 1, so its marker goes on line 1 of the file: # auditme: accept[src-loose-module] <reason>.
  • File-level rules. empty-init-while-siblings-export is accepted by a marker on any line of the __init__.py. phase-section-doc-reference skips a whole file that carries a comment-only line matching # auditme: accept ... phase-section ... (unscoped, with phase-section in the reason).

  • Markdown. A spec-api-signature-drift hit is accepted by the same comment inside the fenced block, on the def line, the line above it, or any line of the signature:

    ```python
# auditme: accept[spec-api-signature-drift] strict lands in the next change
def other(path, strict):
    ...
```

  • AGENTS.md tables. An in-function-import hit is accepted by a table row in the project's AGENTS.md pairing the importer and imported module in backticks, written without a src. prefix (pkg.config.structures). A layering-violation is accepted by a pair in the accepted-exceptions table of the AGENTS.md Package Layering section.

Hits a marker cannot accept

ruff hits come from ruff and are silenced the ruff way (# noqa: <code> or the project's ruff config). lockfile-drift, auditme-check-crash and unreadable-file have no marker either: regenerate the lockfile, fix the checker, or make the file readable. A project can add rules to this list with never-accepted, below.

docs.title: Never-accepted rules
docs.text:
A project that fixes every hit of a rule, and wants no marker to excuse one, lists the rule in pyproject.toml:

[tool.auditme]
never-accepted = ["silent-broad-except", "layering-*"]

Each entry is a rule name, or a family: a name ending in * matches every rule that starts with the text before it (layering-*). The * may appear only at the end. A marker for a listed rule no longer accepts the hit: the hit is reported with accepted false, and the marker's reason is copied into refused_reason, so the reviewer sees what was refused. The hit has to be fixed. An entry that matches no rule exits 2, so a misspelt name cannot leave every marker for that rule counting. never-accepted can sit beside roots in the same table.

Nothing else counts as acceptance: not a prior review, a decision note, or a belief that the pattern is intentional.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
Each rule's predicate, and every carve-out that keeps it from firing, is in the docstring of its check_* function under src/auditor/rules/; the hits auditor check emits itself (see Driver below) have no such docstring. Rules marked gated fire only when the project's AGENTS.md declares the standard they enforce.

Which shared rule each checker rule enforces is listed under "Rules enforced by a check" in the agents repository's rules reference (https://bnomis.github.io/agents/reference/rules/).

docs.title: Driver
docs.text:
Emitted by auditor check itself, not by a registered check.

Rule id Reports src-loose-module A .py file directly in src/, outside any package unreadable-file A file a check could not read (gone, denied or not UTF-8); path names it and evidence is always cannot read <name>, without the reason. The check skips it and reports its other hits. auditme-check-crash A check raised; variant names it and evidence the exception. auditor changed fails on it.

docs.title: duplication.py
docs.text: Rule id Reports literal-duplication The same collection literal (tuple, list, set, frozenset) in several places paired-sibling-helpers Top-level functions with the same body in different files duplicate-side-effect-per-target Several methods of a class calling the same sink with the same self attribute redundant-sink-caller-plus-callee A function calling a sink, then a helper that calls the same sink with the same arguments duplicate-call-sequence Two functions in different classes or modules sharing a long ordered run of calls recompile-duplication A re.compile(...) constant whose name is also compiled in another file

docs.title: error_handling.py
docs.text: Rule id Reports silent-broad-except except Exception with no logger call and no raise broad-except-wrong-level A broad except logging at warning, error, info or debug instead of logger.exception except-interpolation A caught exception interpolated into an f-string or passed as a logger argument mixed-raise-types A function raising both stdlib and project exceptions with no shared base asymmetric-exception-translation A function with no error translation of its own whose every caller wraps it, and whose own body calls something that can raise (filesystem, subprocess or an external module); not one that translates through a same-module translator sibling-errors-no-common-base Error classes in one errors.py that do not share a parent cli-entry-missing-error-envelope A run_* function in cli/*.py with no top-level try/except try-wrapping-with-block-too-broad A try: with X(): whose handler repeats work from the with body layer-has-domain-error-raises-stdlib A module raising a stdlib exception where its package defines domain errors inconsistent-error-translation Callers of one helper translating its error to different project errors filesystem-envelope-gap A try around a filesystem-touching third-party helper whose except omits OSError filesystem-op-without-envelope A public function writing to the filesystem with no try/except logger-exception-graceful-degradation A handler calling logger.exception then returning a constant default docstring-raises-mismatch A docstring Raises: naming a different exception from the one the body raises missing-raises-section A function raising a project error that reaches its caller (not one a handler around it catches without re-raising) whose docstring has no Raises: section bare-except-in-module-with-narrow-errors except Exception in a module that elsewhere catches a narrow *_ERRORS tuple failure-as-absence A clean-absence return (None, empty) reached from a caught exception or a non-200 response get-container-default-then-method-call x = d.get(k, {}) later used as a method receiver: the default does not fire for an explicit null translator-envelope-gap A body whose only error envelope is a translating decorator or context manager with too narrow an except raises-section-drift A Raises: section naming an error that never reaches the caller, or omitting one that does (a callee error guarded only by optional arguments the call leaves unset does not count). Errors are followed through callees with no Raises: section and through Class.method() calls. A combined entry (ParseError, FetchError:) declares each name, and except NAME: naming a module-level tuple of classes catches each member. Callees in libraries that [tool.auditme] first-party lists are followed too

docs.title: imports_and_surfaces.py
docs.text: Rule id Reports def-class-in-init A top-level def or class in an __init__.py in-function-import An import inside a function (variant: stdlib, first-party or third-party), outside TYPE_CHECKING and ImportError guards unused-submodule-import import X.Y.Z never referenced layering-violation A first-party import going up the AGENTS.md package layering (gated) passthrough-shim An undecorated module-level function whose body is only return f(...), passing each of its own parameters once, by name or position empty-init-while-siblings-export A subpackage __init__.py exporting nothing while a sibling exports a substantial surface migration-shim-consumer An import through a re-export shim instead of the symbol's canonical module reexport-in-non-init X = some.module.X at module scope outside an __init__.py annotated-all-assignment __all__: list[str] = [...], which a guard matching plain assignment skips as-import import X as Y or from M import X as Y (gated) from-import from X import Y outside an __init__.py

docs.title: Project hygiene
docs.text: Rule id Reports ruff A ruff check diagnostic (variant: the ruff code), a file ruff format --check would reformat (variant ruff-format, at the line ruff names), ruff missing, or ruff output that is not JSON (ruff-check-parse-error, ruff-format-parse-error) lockfile-drift uv lock --check failing: the lockfile is out of date, or could not be verified ruff-version-drift The ruff the audit runs differs from the ruff-pre-commit rev, or either version cannot be read phase-section-doc-reference A docstring or comment citing Phase N or Section X.Y of a spec spec-api-signature-drift A def in a fenced block under a spec's API heading whose parameters differ from the source

docs.title: state_and_effects.py
docs.text: Rule id Reports constructor-disk-io Disk I/O inside __init__ silent-self-mutation A method other than __post_init__, __setattr__, a setter, clear, reset, update, mutate, merge, replace, apply, patch or override (or a name that is one of these words followed by _ and more, such as update_cache) reassigning an attribute set from a constructor argument return-shadows-instance-attr A method returning a value named like an instance attribute, leaving the caller to reassign it parameter-mutation-in-pure-function A function named or documented as a check that mutates a parameter pure-name-has-side-effect A function with a query-like name opening or reading a file, testing existence, running a subprocess, reading the clock or writing to disk; a registered check_ function is skipped mutable-store-without-copy __init__ storing a dict or list parameter on self without a copy assert-never-missing An if/elif chain, or a match, on string values of one name or dotted name (== or in arms) ending without assert_never; three arms, or two when the subject is annotated Literal[...] with three or more string members build-name-has-side-effect A build_*, compute_* or make_* function calling subprocess, the clock, uuid, random or a filesystem write mutable-module-level-exported A mutable module-level container read by name from another module mutable-members-in-immutable-wrapper An externally read container in a shallow immutable wrapper that still holds mutable members discarded-tuple-return A call, as a bare statement or awaited, to a package function annotated -> tuple[A, B, ...] (two or more element types), so the result is thrown away; _ = f() and a, _ = f() name the discard and tuple[X, ...] is a sequence callback-hotpath-io A Trainer callback method doing filesystem I/O on every event dataclass-optional-always-set A dataclass field typed as optional, defaulting to None, that __post_init__ always sets dead-local-init A local initialised at the top of a function and overwritten on every path before use subprocess-without-memoisation A function with a request-invariant name calling subprocess without a cache decorator

docs.title: style_and_naming.py
docs.text:
The rules from wildcard-imports to leading-underscore-attribute-access, legacy-formatting-percent aside, are regex matches on each non-comment line, except the form of leading-underscore-def-class that finds a def or class nested in a function, which comes from an AST check.

Rule id Reports wildcard-imports from X import * future-annotations from __future__ aliased-imports import X as Y, at any indentation legacy-typing Union[, Optional[, List[, Dict[, Tuple[, Set[, FrozenSet[ or Type[ legacy-formatting-format .format() called on a string literal legacy-formatting-percent %-style formatting in a string literal, strftime directives excepted stdlib-logging An import of the stdlib logging module relative-import-nonpackage A relative import outside an __init__.py leading-underscore-def-class A def or class named _x, at module level or nested in a function leading-underscore-const-upper A module-level _NAME = ... leading-underscore-const-lower A module-level _name = ... leading-underscore-self self._attr leading-underscore-attribute-access obj._attr, in code or a docstring, except public stdlib names such as os._exit leading-underscore-binding A parameter or bound name with a leading underscore underscore-unpack-target-read A _x tuple-unpack target that is read afterwards underscore-forloop-target-read A for _x in ... target read inside the loop non-alphabetical-literal A collection of string members not in alphabetical order (__all__ may instead follow ruff's RUF022 order) non-alphabetical-dict-keys A module-level dict with string keys not in alphabetical order bare-parametric-annotation dict, list, tuple, set or frozenset in an annotation without type parameters, including inside a subscript (list[dict]) bare-nonbuiltin-generic-annotation A parameterisable non-builtin class (collections.deque, queue.Queue, ...) annotated without its parameter typing-deprecated-alias A typing alias deprecated by PEP 585, such as typing.Sequence duplicated-word A word repeated in a comment or string ("the the")

docs.title: Project-level checks
docs.text:
A project-level check asks about the project, not a package, and runs once (PROJECT_CHECKS in registry.py), whatever the number of passes:

  • ruff-version-drift reads .pre-commit-config.yaml and is anchored at the ruff-pre-commit rev: line, where its marker goes. It is silent with no config or no ruff-pre-commit repo; a rev that names no version, and a ruff that cannot run, are hits.
  • lockfile-drift runs only when both pyproject.toml and uv.lock exist, and reports a uv that cannot run as a hit.
  • spec-api-signature-drift reads every Markdown file in scope against the whole corpus, so a per-root pass would repeat it. It fires only when the name resolves to exactly one module-level definition.

Every other check runs once per pass, over that pass's root. Among them, layering-violation, as-import and in-function-import read AGENTS.md for their gate or their acceptance tables, and ruff runs over the pass's root. The driver prints identical hits once.

docs.title: The pinned version and upgrades
docs.text: Projects pin the auditme-changed and auditme-all hooks to a revision of this repository, so a new rule never fails a build until the project chooses to upgrade. Upgrading can surface hits in code that passed before; fix or accept them in the same commit as the upgrade. The commands are in Upgrading the checker, and installing and adopting the hooks is covered in Setting up the shared guards.

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: claude/skills/auditme/SKILL.md covers the rest of the skill: the interpretive review that follows the sweep, the review and summary templates, the convergence rules, and how to add or narrow a check.

docs.title: Command line and hooks
docs.text: Reference for the scripts in this repository and the hooks it publishes. For installation see Setup; for what the checker's rules report see The checker.

docs.title: bin/install-claude.sh
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh [--dry-run] [any other install-in-claude option]

Links the contents of claude/ into ~/.claude/, and registers the Stop hook, by running the shared installer install-in-claude at the commit pinned in the script's INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV:

uvx --from "git+ssh://git@github.com/bnomis/install-in-claude.git@$INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV" \
    install-in-claude --source "$REPO/claude" \
    --append 'hooks.Stop[auditme-stop.sh]={"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"bash \"$HOME/.claude/hooks/auditme-stop.sh\""}]}'

Its own arguments pass through: bin/install-claude.sh --dry-run prints what would change and changes nothing. It needs uv, and SSH access to bnomis/install-in-claude for the first run of a pinned commit; uvx caches it after that. The shared rules, the other skills and the status line are installed by the agents repository's own installer.

What the installer does, in short (its README has the detail):

  • Checks every option and reads ~/.claude/settings.json first; a settings file that is not a valid JSON object stops it, exit 1, before anything is linked or written.
  • For each top-level entry of claude/ (dotfiles skipped): a file becomes a symlink in ~/.claude/; a directory (hooks/, rules/, skills/) becomes a real directory in ~/.claude/ whose entries are symlinks, so ~/.claude/skills/auditme links to claude/skills/auditme/. Links are relative. An existing symlink is replaced; an existing file is renamed with a .orig suffix (numbered when that name is taken).
  • Prints any dangling symlinks in ~/.claude/ and its immediate subdirectories, with a quoted rm command to remove them. It does not remove them.
  • Adds the Stop hook entry to ~/.claude/settings.json unless a Stop entry already names auditme-stop.sh. Every other key and hook is kept; the first original is copied to settings.json.orig; the file is written atomically and keeps its mode.
Exit Meaning 0 Installed, or nothing to do 1 settings.json is not valid JSON or not a JSON object, a key on the edit path is not an object, or hooks.Stop is not a list; nothing changed 2 A bad argument; nothing changed

Environment: HOME.

To upgrade the installer, set INSTALL_IN_CLAUDE_REV to a newer commit (git ls-remote git@github.com:bnomis/install-in-claude.git refs/heads/main, first field) and run bin/install-claude.sh --dry-run to see what it changes.

docs.title: bin/install-hooks.sh
docs.text:
bin/install-hooks.sh [--rev <commit>] [--push] [--no-install] [--dry-run] [<repo-path>]

Installs the audit hooks in another git repository, or moves them to a newer commit of this one, by editing that repository's .pre-commit-config.yaml, then installs its git hooks. <repo-path> is any path inside the repository; the default is the current directory. Run it again whenever you want the latest checker: a second run at the same commit changes nothing.

What it does to .pre-commit-config.yaml:

  • No file: writes one holding only the auditor entry.
  • No auditor entry: adds one at the end of the repos: list (before any top-level key that follows the list), indented like the list's first entry:
- repo: https://github.com/bnomis/auditor
  rev: <commit>
  hooks:
    - id: auditme-changed
    - id: auditme-all
  • An auditor entry (by git@github.com:bnomis/auditor.git or https://github.com/bnomis/auditor, with or without .git): sets its rev: to the commit, dropping any comment on that line, moves its repo: to https://github.com/bnomis/auditor (which CI clones without a key), and adds auditme-changed or auditme-all if the entry lacks one. Every other line, the entry's stages: and args: included, stays as it was.

Then, unless --no-install or --dry-run, it runs pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push in the repository. When pre-commit is on PATH the new file is checked with pre-commit validate-config before it replaces the old one.

Option Effect --rev <commit> Pin this commit (7 to 40 hex digits) instead of the current main of bnomis/auditor, read with git ls-remote https://github.com/bnomis/auditor refs/heads/main --push When it adds auditme-all, give it stages: [manual, pre-push], so every push sweeps the whole tree. Leave it off for a project that still has unaccepted hits (see An existing project); an auditme-all already in the file keeps its stages --no-install Edit the file only; do not run pre-commit install --dry-run Print the change as a unified diff and change nothing Exit Meaning 0 Installed or updated, already at the commit, or a dry run 1 Nothing changed, because: main of bnomis/auditor could not be read; pre-commit is needed and not installed; the file pins the audit hooks from bnomis/agents (move it first, see Moving a project from agents); it has more than one auditor entry, no block-style top-level repos: list, or an auditor entry with no hooks: list; or the new file fails pre-commit validate-config 2 A bad argument, a --rev that is not a commit hash, or a path that is not in a git repository; nothing changed

It does not add the CI step: /auditme-project-setup does that (see An existing project). The CI step needs no key, since the hooks clone over HTTPS from a public repository.

docs.title: bin/check-foreign-names.sh
docs.text:
check-foreign-names.sh [--allow=<name>]... [--] <file>...

Fails when a file names a project on a list kept outside the repository, so that the list itself is never committed. It is the entry of the no-project-names hook and changes nothing on disk.

  • The list is one name per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped.
  • Matching is whole-word, case-insensitive and literal (grep -w -i -F): a name inside a longer word does not match.
  • --allow=<name> removes that name from the list for this run (compared case-insensitively against whole lines). Repeatable. A repository used across projects passes its own name this way.
  • Each match is printed as file:line:text, followed by a pointer to claude/rules/rule-scope.md in the agents repository.
Exit Meaning 0 No match; or nothing exists at the list path (a notice goes to stderr and nothing is checked); or the list is empty after comments and --allow; or no files given 1 At least one match, even when another file is unreadable (a message naming it goes to stderr) 2 Something exists at the list path but it cannot be read as a file (a directory, or no read permission) (check-foreign-names: cannot read <list> on stderr), whatever the files; or no match, but a file could not be read (a message naming it goes to stderr)

Environment: AUDITOR_FOREIGN_NAMES (path of the list), HOME (the default list is ~/.config/auditor/foreign-names).

docs.title: auditor check
docs.text:
auditor check [-h] [--package PACKAGE] [--extra-root DIR] scope

The checker driver. Runs every registered check over the project at scope and prints one JSON object per hit on stdout. It reads the tree and writes nothing.

Option Effect scope Project root. --package PACKAGE Audit only src/PACKAGE, which must be a directory name directly under src/ (a path or .. exits 2). Drops the extra roots and the loose-module check. For re-checking one package; a normal audit passes neither option. --extra-root DIR Audit DIR (relative to scope) as its own pass, as a package root. Repeatable. Replaces the default extra root, bin/, and replaces any roots declared in [tool.auditme] for that run; each named directory must exist and resolve inside scope (one outside exits 2).

Without options it audits every package under src/, each in its own pass, then bin/ when it exists and holds .py files. A .py file directly in src/ is reported as src-loose-module. A project with neither, such as one with no Python, still gets the project-level checks, once: the lockfile (lockfile-drift), the ruff pin (ruff-version-drift) and spec-api-signature-drift over the project's Markdown.

docs.title: Declared roots
docs.text:
A project whose Python is not under src/<package>/ and bin/ declares its roots in pyproject.toml:

[tool.auditme]
roots = [
    { path = "tools/mypkg" },
    { path = "tools", modules = "top-level" },
]
Key Meaning path Required. A directory relative to scope that holds at least one .py file. modules "package" (the default) or "top-level".

A package root is swept recursively and its modules are named after the root (tools/mypkg/core.py is mypkg.core). A top-level root is a directory on sys.path: only the .py files directly in it are swept, each named by its stem, and its subdirectories are left to their own roots, so a package inside it is declared as a package root of its own.

The declared list replaces the default roots, in the order given: a project that also has src/ packages lists them. With no [tool.auditme] table, or no pyproject.toml, the defaults apply. --extra-root replaces the declared list for one run. A declared root that resolves outside the project is an invalid declaration. No two package roots may nest, and no top-level root may sit inside a package root. The hooks and the Phase B listers read the same list.

docs.title: First-party libraries
docs.text:
raises-section-drift follows a call into a first-party library only when the project lists the library's package directory:

[tool.auditme]
first-party = ["../lib/src/lib"]

Each entry is a directory named as its import name (../lib/src/lib for import lib), relative to the project. It may lie outside the project. The rule reads its Raises: sections and error classes, so an error the library declares counts as a domain error, but never sweeps it: no hit is reported on its files. A listed directory must exist wherever the sweep runs, CI included, or the sweep stops with the errors below. Nothing is inferred from [tool.uv.sources] or the environment.

docs.title: Never-accepted rules
docs.text:
never-accepted lists rules whose accept markers a project refuses:

[tool.auditme]
never-accepted = ["silent-broad-except", "layering-*"]

Each entry is a rule name, or a family ending in * (the * only at the end). A hit of a listed rule is reported with accepted false and the marker's reason in refused_reason; a hit with no marker carries no refused_reason. auditor changed names the setting in its advice for such a hit. The key can sit beside roots.

Each output line carries rule, variant, path, line, evidence, accepted and accepted_reason; a hit from a rule that compares several files also carries related, the other files involved. Identical hits are printed once. A check that raises is reported as an auditme-check-crash hit, and the sweep continues.

Exit Meaning 0 Sweep completed, whatever it found; also when there is no root to audit (a notice goes to stderr and only the project-level checks run) 2 scope is not a directory; --package is not a plain directory name, or its directory does not exist or is a file; a named --extra-root is outside scope or is not a directory; an argument error (argparse's usage message on stderr); AUDITME_RUFF is set to something that is not an executable file (ERROR: AUDITME_RUFF=<value> is not an executable file); or an invalid [tool.auditme] declaration, printed as ERROR: <message> on stderr with nothing on stdout (see below)

The declaration errors, each exit 2:

Message Cause pyproject.toml: not valid TOML (<parse error>) pyproject.toml is not valid TOML and mentions [tool.auditme pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: must be a table [tool.auditme] is not a table pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: unknown key '<key>' a key other than roots, first-party or never-accepted pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: never-accepted must be a list of strings never-accepted is not a list of strings pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: never-accepted '<pattern>' may use * only at the end a * anywhere but the last character pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: never-accepted '<pattern>' matches no rule id a name or family that matches no rule pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: roots must be a list of tables roots is not a list of tables pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: unknown key '<key>' in a roots entry an entry has a key other than path or modules pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: a roots entry has no path an entry lacks path pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: modules must be 'package' or 'top-level', not '<value>' an invalid modules declared root <path> not found the directory does not exist declared root <path> holds no .py file no .py file (for top-level, none directly in it) declared roots <a> and <b> overlap two roots would sweep a file twice declared root <path> is outside the project the path resolves outside scope, as an absolute path or .. does pyproject.toml [tool.auditme]: first-party must be a list of strings first-party is not a list of non-empty strings first-party path <path> not found the entry does not exist or is not a directory first-party path <path> holds no .py file no .py file in the directory first-party path <path> lies inside a root the sweep audits the entry is inside a swept root

The hooks treat any of these as a sweep that cannot run, and auditor phaseb exits 2 with the same message.

auditor phaseb exits 2 for a --question that is not a registered question, on every subcommand, before it builds a ledger path, and for a <root> that does not exist or is not a directory, so a mistyped root never reads as an empty listing.

It also exits 2, printing phaseb.py: and the error's message to stderr, whenever a Phase B step fails: for example a merge for a run planned for another question, or a merge whose batches fail check.

auditor phaseb plan records the callee depth it listed at (--depth, default 3) in plan.json. auditor phaseb merge exits 2, naming both depths and writing nothing to the ledger, when its own --depth differs from the plan's: merge with the plan's depth, or plan again. A plan.json written before the depth was recorded is read as depth 3.

--depth is accepted by candidates, plan, merge and report, only for the questions that follow callees (A4, T1 and T2), and must be at least 1. For any other question, or a value below 1, the command exits 2 with a usage error.

The exit status does not reflect hits: callers read stdout.

Environment: the checks run ruff and uv as subprocesses with the caller's environment, finding them through PATH (ruff from $AUDITME_RUFF when set, else the project's .venv/bin/ruff, first). AUDITME_RUFF is the path of an executable ruff; auditor check exits 2 when it names anything else. When uv lock --check fails because of a user-level exclude-newer setting, it is rerun with UV_NO_CONFIG set.

docs.title: auditor rules
docs.text:
Reports on the rules repository that AUDITOR_RULES_PATH names. Every command prints ERROR: ... and exits non-zero when the variable is unset or the repository is invalid.

auditor rules list [--kind {check,project-check,question,standard}]
auditor rules check
auditor rules test [pytest args]
auditor rules standards
auditor rules questions [--category {A,D,Doc,P,S,Sec,T}]
auditor rules identity [--expect <json-file>]
auditor rules pending
auditor rules init <dest> [--pack P ...]
auditor rules apply <dest>
auditor rules packs
Command What it does Exit status list One line per rule: name, kind, what it emits or its id, title 0 check Imports every entry file; reports imports outside the helper API package non-zero on a bad import test Runs pytest over rules/*/tests with the auditor.testing plugin; extra arguments go to pytest pytest's standards Prints every standard rule's rule.md, in name order 0 questions Prints the Phase B checklist: id, title and rule.md of each question 0 identity Prints the runner and rules identity as JSON; the audit skill records it in each review with --expect, 1 when it differs from the file pending Lists the open items (the ## headings) of the rules repository's TODO.md 1 when an item is open init <dest> Writes <dest>/selection.txt: every rule of the catalogue, grouped by pack; the rules of each --pack named start uncommented, and with no --pack every pack does. Needs no rules repository 2 on an error, with <dest> unchanged apply <dest> Copies the rules left uncommented in <dest>/selection.txt, with their tests, into <dest>/rules, writes the repository files, runs git init unless <dest> is already in a work tree, then runs check on the result. Needs no rules repository 2 on an error, with <dest> unchanged packs One line per pack: name, rule count, description. Needs no rules repository 0

auditor check and auditor phaseb load the same repository and run its rules in rule-name order.

docs.title: auditor changed
docs.text:
auditor changed [-h] [--all] [--scope] [--base BASE] [repo_root]

The entry of the auditme-changed and auditme-all hooks. Runs auditor check over the whole tree with the same interpreter (timeout 600 seconds), then reports every unaccepted hit in scope. It writes nothing.

Option Effect repo_root Repository root. Default: git rev-parse --show-toplevel of the working directory. --all Report every unaccepted hit, not only those in changed files. --scope Run no sweep. Print one JSON line per changed .py or .sh file, {"path": ..., "ranges": [[start, end], ...]}: the lines changed since the merge base of BASE and HEAD (index and working tree included), each Python hunk widened to its enclosing function, else its enclosing class; shell hunks are kept as they are. A deleted file is not listed. Exit 0; with no diff base, a message on stderr and exit 0. --base BASE Diff base. Default: the first of @{upstream}, origin/main, main that resolves. A value starting with - is refused, whatever spelling of the option gave it (an abbreviation such as --bas=, or a repeat), and git is told where options end before it is passed the range.

Without --all, the scope is the files changed in BASE...HEAD plus those changed in the index or working tree against HEAD, deletions excluded. A hit is in scope when its path or any of its related paths is in scope, so a cross-file hit on an untouched file fails when its peer changes.

Without --all, the sweep is skipped (exit 0, with a message) when:

  • no diff base resolves; or
  • no changed file is reportable: a .py file, a uv.lock, or a .md file outside hidden directories and outside .git, .venv, node_modules, __pycache__, audit-reviews and tasks.

Each reported hit prints as path:line rule with its variant indented beneath, then how to accept a hit (a ruff, lockfile-drift or never-accepted hit gets its own advice instead, as no accept marker applies to any of them) and how to skip the hook once (SKIP=auditme-changed git commit, or SKIP=auditme-all git push with --all). All output goes to stdout, except argparse's usage errors and the no-diff-base message of --scope, which go to stderr.

Exit Meaning 0 No unaccepted hit in scope; the sweep was skipped as above; or --help 1 An unaccepted hit in scope; or any failure: argument error, --base refused, git failed, --scope cannot read a changed Python file, the sweep timed out, exited non-zero, printed a line that is not a JSON object, or reported a crashed check (even one outside the scope); or the audit sweep could not start, or the repository root could not be resolved

Environment: none directly; git and auditor check inherit the caller's.

docs.title: Published pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
.pre-commit-hooks.yaml publishes these hooks for other repositories to pin by rev. This repository runs the same entries from its own tree as repo: local hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml, so a checker change applies in the commit that makes it.

Hook id Stages as published Entry Checks In this repository auditme-changed [pre-commit] auditor changed Unaccepted checker hits in the files the change touches Same stage auditme-all [manual] auditor changed --all Unaccepted checker hits anywhere [manual, pre-push]: runs on every push no-project-names [pre-commit, commit-msg] bin/check-foreign-names.sh Project names in staged files and the commit message; uv.lock excluded Same stages, no --allow

Both audit hooks set pass_filenames: false and always_run: true: they find their own scope and run even when no file is staged. no-project-names receives the staged file names, or the commit message file at commit-msg; a repository used across projects pins it with its own names as args: [--allow=<name>], and installs the commit-msg hook type (pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg). The audit hooks use language: python, so pre-commit installs this repository's auditor package into the hook's own environment and runs auditor changed from it. no-project-names uses language: script, so its entry runs from the hook repository with bash.

To run the manual hook by hand:

pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files

This repository's config also runs ruff-check, ruff-format and shellcheck; those come from their own repositories and are not published here.

docs.title: The Stop hook
docs.text:
claude/hooks/auditme-stop.sh is a Claude Code Stop hook: Claude Code runs it when Claude is about to end a turn, with the event JSON on stdin.

It does nothing (exit 0, no output) when:

  • the payload's stop_hook_active is true, meaning the turn is already continuing because of an earlier block, so it blocks at most once in a row;
  • the working directory is not in a git repository;
  • the project is not opted in: its root .pre-commit-config.yaml does not contain the text id: auditme-changed.

Otherwise it runs the installed checker, not the project's pinned one, from the repository root:

auditor changed

The exception is a worktree of the auditor repository itself: when the git directory that bin/install-claude.sh recorded in ~/.claude/auditor-source is the project's own shared git directory and the project holds src/auditor/cli.py, the hook runs uv run --project <root> auditor changed instead, so a branch that changes the checker is judged by that branch. Any other repository's src/auditor is never run.

When that exits 1 it prints {"decision": "block", "reason": "<report>"}, and Claude Code keeps the turn going with the report as the reason. Since auditor changed exits 1 on a failed sweep as well as on hits, a sweep that cannot run also blocks.

It also blocks when the checker never ran, so a broken install cannot turn the audit off without a word:

  • when auditor is not on PATH (and the project is not a trusted worktree), it blocks once, saying the auditor CLI is not installed; run bin/install-claude.sh in this repository to install it;
  • when auditor changed exits with any status other than 0 or 1 (for example 127 for no uv), it blocks with the status and the output.

As with every block, it blocks at most once in a row. The hook itself always exits 0 and writes nothing to disk.

Requires jq, git and auditor on PATH (and uv for a trusted worktree). Environment: HOME.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
bin/install-claude.sh adds it once to ~/.claude/settings.json:

{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "bash \"$HOME/.claude/hooks/auditme-stop.sh\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

It is global, but acts only in opted-in projects. Check it with grep -n 'auditme-stop.sh' ~/.claude/settings.json.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
The Python standards the auditme checker enforces are standard rules of the default rules catalogue, src/auditor/catalogue/rules/std-*/, one directory per section. auditor rules standards prints them, and the SessionStart hook (claude/hooks/auditme-standards.sh) puts them in the context of a session in a project that opts in. They sit beside the rules the agents repository installs (bnomis/agents, https://bnomis.github.io/agents/reference/rules/).

A check's rule.toml lists the standards it enforces in its standards key.

Standards sections Require std-python-version, std-critical-rules, std-type-annotations, std-naming, std-no-leading-underscores, std-string-formatting, std-alphabetical-ordering, std-clean-init-py-files, std-logging and the rest of the coding standards Python 3.14; ruff as configured; full type annotations with built-in generics and \| unions; no leading underscores; f-strings; alphabetical ordering of enum-like collections; nothing defined in __init__.py; loguru for logging. std-commands, std-the-lockfile, std-dependencies-python-version Declare dependencies in pyproject.toml via uv add; commit uv.lock and never hand-edit it; no pip install. std-imports-in-init-files, std-no-as-imports Full import paths (no from X import Y outside __init__.py re-exports), no as imports, no wildcard imports, no from __future__ import annotations.

docs.title: Rules enforced by a check
docs.text: The checks below run as this repository's pre-commit hooks or as rules of the auditme checker; The audit checker says what each checker rule reports and how to accept a hit. rule-scope.md, git-conventions.md and python/asserts.md are rules of the agents repository; the others are the rules above. No hook or checker rule checks any other rule.

docs.title: rule-scope.md
docs.text: The no-project-names hook fails a file or a commit message that names a project on a list kept outside the repository. It runs at the pre-commit and commit-msg stages, both as published and in this repository's own config.

docs.title: git-conventions.md
docs.text: The requirement that a script-checkable rule be a hook is met by the auditme-changed hook at pre-commit and auditme-all at pre-push, plus the ruff and shellcheck hooks a project's .pre-commit-config.yaml pins. Nothing checks commit message format or branch names.

docs.title: Coding standards (std-* sections)
docs.text: Requirement Checker rule Follow the project's ruff configuration ruff (runs ruff check and ruff format --check with the project's config), ruff-version-drift (the ruff the audit runs differs from the ruff hook's rev) No leading underscores leading-underscore-def-class, leading-underscore-const-upper, leading-underscore-const-lower, leading-underscore-self, leading-underscore-attribute-access, leading-underscore-binding, underscore-forloop-target-read, underscore-unpack-target-read f-strings legacy-formatting-percent, legacy-formatting-format Built-in generics and \| unions legacy-typing, typing-deprecated-alias, bare-parametric-annotation, bare-nonbuiltin-generic-annotation No from __future__ import annotations future-annotations loguru, not stdlib logging stdlib-logging Nothing defined in __init__.py def-class-in-init Alphabetical ordering non-alphabetical-literal, non-alphabetical-dict-keys

docs.title: Import standards (std-imports-in-init-files, std-no-as-imports)
docs.text: Requirement Checker rule Full import paths from-import, relative-import-nonpackage No wildcard imports wildcard-imports No as imports aliased-imports; also as-import, which fires only when the project's AGENTS.md declares the ban No from __future__ import annotations future-annotations

docs.title: Dependency standards (std-commands, std-the-lockfile)
docs.text: lockfile-drift runs uv lock --check when the project has both pyproject.toml and uv.lock, and reports a lockfile that no longer matches pyproject.toml.

docs.title: python/asserts.md
docs.text: No checker rule. Ruff reports assert as S101 in a project whose ruff config selects the S (bandit) rules, and the checker's ruff rule passes that hit through.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Each skill is a directory under claude/skills/<name>/ holding a SKILL.md and any scripts or templates it uses. bin/install-claude.sh links claude/skills/ into ~/.claude/skills/, so each skill is available in every project as ~/.claude/skills/<name>/. The other shared skills are in the agents repository (bnomis/agents, https://bnomis.github.io/agents/).

Invoke a skill in Claude Code as /<name> [args], or by asking for what it does: the when_to_use list in each skill's frontmatter names the phrases that trigger it ("audit the code", "set up a new project").

Skill Invocation Purpose auditme /auditme [scope] Scripted and checklist audit of code, specs and docs auditme-project-setup /auditme-project-setup new [path], /auditme-project-setup adopt [path] Install the shared audit hooks, CI gate and project files

docs.title: /auditme
docs.text:
/auditme [scope] [--category <category>]

Scope is empty (specs, src/, bin/, docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md), a file path, a spec slug, or the docs. --category (standards, architecture, performance, security, testing, dependencies, documentation) is a debugging aid; a normal audit runs every category.

  • Runs: the scripted sweep auditor check <project-root>, then a fixed checklist (a listed question runs one reviewer per batch of its candidates; a sampled question runs on the lines changed since the previous review, each widened to its enclosing function, and on the whole tree every third audit and on any audit with no previous **Commit:**), then a spec review and re-verification of earlier findings.
  • Refuses to start while auditor rules pending reports open change requests in the rules repository's TODO.md.
  • Writes: agents/audit-reviews/review-N.md, agents/audit-reviews/summary.md, agents/audit-reviews/index.md, the Phase B ledger (agents/audit-reviews/ledger/<question>.jsonl), and marks shipped tasks done in agents/tasks/audit-reviews/.
  • Then: runs /taskdev agents/audit-reviews/review-N.md if there are findings.
  • Stops for: uncommitted changes; commit (docs(audit): add review-N).

The checker, its rules and accept markers are described in The checker.

docs.title: /auditme-project-setup
docs.text:
/auditme-project-setup new [<path>]
/auditme-project-setup adopt [<path>]

Path defaults to the current repository root. Templates are in claude/skills/auditme-project-setup/templates/.

  • new: writes .pre-commit-config.yaml (ruff, shellcheck, and the auditme-changed and auditme-all hooks pinned to this repository's current main commit), .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, TODO.md, DONE.md and claude/rules/README.md; installs the pre-commit and pre-push hooks. Asks before overwriting an existing .pre-commit-config.yaml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md, TODO.md or DONE.md.
  • adopt: adds the auditme hooks, offers to remove a project-local hook doing the same job, and counts unaccepted hits with pre-commit run auditme-all --hook-stage manual --all-files. At zero hits it enables the pre-push stage and adds the CI audit step; otherwise it files a dated TODO.md item instead and enables neither gate.
  • Stops for: the project name and test command; a failing git ls-remote of the auditor repository (no network access); overwriting an existing project file (new); removing a project-local hook (adopt); commit. Never pushes. CI needs no key or secret: the hooks clone the public auditor repository over HTTPS.

See Setup for the full walk-through.
